excerpt: The cutter that does most of the work in relief carving, explained: why the taper matters, what each tip size can and cannot render, the stepover that goes with it, feeds for a hobby machine, why straight ball noses snap, and the three-cutter set that covers everything.
seo_title: Tapered Ball Nose Bits for CNC Relief Carving: Tip Size, Stepover, Feeds
seo_description: How to choose tapered ball nose bits for 3D relief carving: 1/16, 1/32, 1 mm and 0.5 mm tips and the detail each renders, stepover by tip, taper angle and wall limits, feeds and RPM for hobby routers, why they break, and a starter set.

email.subject: The one cutter that decides how your relief carving looks
email.intro:
Every relief carving is finished by a tapered ball nose, and most of the questions we get (fuzz, blur, a snapped bit at hour three, a face that will not resolve) come back to which one was in the collet and how it was driven.

The new guide covers the cutter from the ground up: why the taper matters, what each tip size can actually render, the stepover and feed that go with it, why straight ball noses snap, and the three cutters that cover every file in the catalogue.
